A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WOFTRL research work. Their main text, equations, three figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1, 5.2, and 6.1 report original simulations of Matching Pennies, Sato's game, and weighted Rock-Paper-Scissors in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Sections 5.1, 5.2, and 6.1 and Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 8's WOFTRL update remains unchanged. The conclusion adds a suggested adaptation for bounded stochastic delays: choose n above all possible delays and consistently use feedback n−1 steps old. This changes feedback selection for the proposed extension but is not experimentally evaluated.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Matching Pennies, nonzero-sum Sato's game, and weighted zero-sum Rock-Paper-Scissors. The added stochastic-delay discussion does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The same optimistic-weight comparisons, including OFTRL at n=1, appear in the corresponding experiments. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The games, regularizers, regret metric, parameter sweeps, and experimental learning rates are retained. Figure 3 still uses m=4, eta=0.1, and n=3,4,5,6. Revised theoretical learning-rate conditions do not establish changes to the simulation protocols.

E4.justification: The delay-versus-optimism phase diagrams, learning-rate scaling comparisons, and convergence trajectories are unchanged. The revised appendices add mathematical analyses, not new empirical ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the simulations. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The graphics in Figures 1–3 are identical, and their reported empirical trends and outcomes are retained. Renaming total regret as social regret does not change the measured quantity or results.

T1.justification: Corollary 13 replaces best-iterate convergence with last-iterate convergence, supported by a substantially rewritten Appendix E introducing a Lyapunov function. New Appendix F derives an O(m^(3/2)T^(1/4)) individual-regret bound. The RVU definition becomes explicitly per-player, its negative variation coefficient changes from 1/(8 eta) to 1/(4 eta), and Corollary 11's learning rate and bound change. The stated Lipschitz constant is also revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion strengthen the central convergence claim from convergence along a subsequence to convergence of the entire iterate sequence. They also explicitly identify social regret and foreground its quadratic delay dependence, which was already implicit through lambda in v1.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds an applicability argument for bounded stochastic delays. Last-iterate convergence is removed from future work, while obtaining convergence rates becomes an open direction. The explanations of the retained simulation behavior largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds a code-repository access link, absent from v1. The disclosed operating system, Python version, processor, and memory remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes Cai et al.'s work on separating best-, random-, and last-iterate convergence and adds Rockafellar's Convex Analysis. It also explicitly grounds the new convergence argument in the already-cited optimistic mirror-descent work. The broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Terminology is edited throughout to distinguish social and individual regret. Proof exposition gains steps and subsections, and the existing FTRL–mirror-descent equivalence moves from Appendix F into Appendix E. The main section sequence and most introductory and experimental exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain identical graphics. Captions for Figures 1–2 adopt social-regret terminology, equations are regrouped, and text reflows around revised proofs and acknowledgments. There are no added figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves regret distinctions, adds an individual-regret derivation, and supplies code access. Its potentially largest gain is the stronger last-iterate guarantee. However, Appendix E applies Lemma A6's interior-only continuity at a subsequential limit shown merely to lie in X (A97–A99), without resolving the boundary case. Because this leaves the decisive stronger claim incompletely justified as written, the net quality improvement cannot be judged reliably.
